05. Pipeline

From Sensors to Decisions — the Digital Twin

1. Sense

IoT sensors, meters & cameras capture the city.

2. Ingest

Streaming pipelines clean & buffer the feeds.

3. Store

Big-data lakes hold history at city scale.

4. Analyse

ML models forecast, classify & detect.

5. Decide

Dashboards & rules turn output into choices.

6. Act

Actuators & services change the city — then we sense again.

Closed-loop city · sense → act → sense

09. Overview

What is Data Science?

In a smart city, data science sits at the intersection of three core domains:

  • Coding & Hacking: Ability to script, scrape, clean, and run code.
  • Math & Stats: Understanding models, probability, and inference.
  • Domain Expertise: The business context or scientific application.

15. Preprocessing

Outlier Detection & Treatment

Detection Methods

- Z-Score: Out of range of 3 standard deviations (μ ± 3σ).
- IQR Range: Outside the fence limits [Q1 - 1.5×IQR, Q3 + 1.5×IQR].

Treatment Strategies

- Trimming: Deleting extreme rows completely from records.
- Winsorizing: Capping outliers to limit boundary fences (represented below).

Figure 8.1: Detecting outliers via IQR limit lines and capping them (Winsorizing).
16. Scaling

Data Scaling & Normalization

Machine learning models perform better when features are on the same scale. Select a scaling method to visualize how points map onto their new boundaries:

Raw Features

Unscaled values. If features have vastly different ranges (e.g. income vs age), distance-based models (KNN, SVM) will be dominated by the larger range.

Feature Space Plot (Income vs Experience)

Categorical Variables

One-Hot Encoding

Recommended

Creates dummy binary columns. Prevents models from assuming an ordering rank.

is_Red 1
is_Blue 0
is_Green 0
Vector: [1, 0, 0]

Ordinal / Label Encoding

Maps categories directly to integers. Useful only if there is natural order (e.g. Rating).

Integer Rank: 0

Supervised Learning

A supervised model learns from labelled examples (X → y). The shape of y decides the task. Flip between the two:

The model draws a best-fit line minimising squared error, then predicts a number for any new X (house price, temperature, demand).

27. Supervised

Linear Regression

Minimize the Mean Squared Error (MSE): MSE = (1/n) * Σ(y_i - ŷ_i)². Example: predicting a district's energy demand from temperature.

28. Supervised

Logistic Regression

Probability Mapping: Sigmoid

P(y=1) = 1 / (1 + e^(-(w·x + b)))

Maps prediction scores to output probabilities between 0 and 1. Weights (w) control the slope gradient, while bias (b) shifts the threshold position.

Weight (w): 1.0
Bias (b): 0.0
Decision Boundary (P=0.5) at x = 0.0

29. Ensembles

Decision Trees & Random Forests

Decision Trees

Splits features using axis-parallel partition boundaries to maximize Information Gain (reducing local entropy or Gini impurity). Deep trees overfit easily.

Random Forests (Ensembles)

Trains multiple decision trees independently on random bootstrap data subsets (bagging) and feature partitions, averaging predictions to reduce overall model variance.

Figure 22.1: Orthogonal feature space splits (left) and corresponding hierarchical splits structure (right).
30. Regression metrics

Evaluating Regression

Evaluate performance by checking residuals (error margins $y - \hat{y}$). Click in the grid to add points and see how metrics update:

Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
Formula: $$\text{MAE} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n |y_i - \hat{y}_i|$$

Calculates the average magnitude of absolute error differences. Treats all errors equally.

Regression Residuals Visualizer

K-Means Clustering

Groups data by iteratively adjusting K centroids until convergence — e.g. segmenting city zones or households by energy-use pattern.

34. Compression

Principal Component Analysis

PCA: Variance Maximization

Finds orthogonal axes (principal components) that maximize data variance. Projecting high-dimensional data onto the top components preserves maximum information content.

Projection Angle: 0°
Projected Variance: 0%
Tip: Rotate to ~45° (max variance / PC1) or ~135° (min variance / PC2).
Projection of 2D data onto rotated principal component axis
Interactive Projection Canvas
35. Outlier Models

Anomaly Detection

Identifying unusual data instances that deviate significantly from normal trends. In a smart city: detecting power-grid faults, water leaks, failing sensors, and fraud or intrusion alerts.

Unsupervised Algorithms

- Isolation Forests: Isolates anomalies by random attribute splitting.
- One-Class SVM: Estimates densities to encase normal points.
- Local Outlier Factor (LOF): Checks density relative to nearest neighbors.

Figure 28.1: Contour density thresholds isolating low-density anomalies.

37. Ethics & Summary

Ethics & Conclusion

Best Practices:

  • Verify model explainability (SHAP/LIME) on sensitive datasets.
  • Avoid leakage: do preprocessing inside cross-validation splits.
  • Always monitor production metrics for feature and target drift.
